sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 5.2(ii), p.956, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021), 943–966 (Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF, SHA-256 77ff3290…790e)
sourceIssues.printed: "(ii) The number of supersingular points in X₀(N)(F_{p²}) that correspond to supersingular elliptic curves over F_{p²} with the Frobenius trace a_{p²} = 2p or −2p and the j-invariant different from 0 and 1728 is at least µ(⌊(p−1)/12⌋ − 3/2 + (−3/p) + ½(−1/p)). In particular, there is a supersingular point with a_{p²} = 2p or −2p in X₀(N)(F_{p²}) over X(1)(F_{p²})∖{0,1728} that is unramified for π if p ≡ 1 mod 12 or p ≥ 31."
sourceIssues.correction: The displayed bound is valid, but at p = 47 it equals 0, so the "in particular" does not follow from it. The "in particular" is nevertheless true, and for every p ≥ 13. By the Eichler–Deuring count and the N(t) table in the proof, each of the ⌊(p−1)/12⌋ supersingular j ≠ 0, 1728 has models over F_{p²} with a_{p²} = ±2p and µ points of X_0(N)(F_{p²}) above it. That gives µ⌊(p−1)/12⌋ ≥ µ > µ/6 such points. The displayed bound equals µ(⌊(p−1)/12⌋ − 2δ − ε) in the notation p − 1 = 12m + 4δ + 6ε of the proof, and is weaker than this count.
sourceIssues.reason: The deduction needs the lower bound to exceed the number of ramification points, which (i) bounds by µ/6. At p = 47: ⌊46/12⌋ = 3, (−3/47) = −1 and (−1/47) = −1, so the displayed bound is µ(3 − 3/2 − 1 − 1/2) = 0 < µ/6. Every other prime p ≥ 31 passes. The count from the proof's own facts is 3µ at p = 47, so the statement holds and only the deduction from the displayed bound fails. The construction of §5 (p.957) cites Lemma 5.2(ii) and (iii) together, and Rubin's verification (Remark 2.3) covers p = 47, so nothing downstream is affected. Found by the review REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21. Reclassified by REV-ERRATA-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21 from "error; affects a stated result".

review.reason: Checked at p.956 of the Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF (SHA-256 77ff3290…790e, the version named). The arithmetic is right: at p = 47 the displayed bound is 0, so the "in particular" does not follow from it. This review corrects the reach in place. The entry called this a false stated result, but the "in particular" is true, including at p = 47. The facts in the paper's own proof (p.957) give more than the displayed bound. Write p − 1 = 12m + 4δ + 6ε. The N(t) table gives N(2p) = N(−2p) = m + δ + ε, and the classes with t = ±p and t = 0 occur only for j = 0 and j = 1728. So each of the m = ⌊(p−1)/12⌋ supersingular j-invariants other than 0 and 1728 has models over F_{p²} with a_{p²} = ±2p. Each has µ points of X_0(N)(F_{p²}) above it, by étaleness and Lemma 5.1(i). The true count is therefore µ⌊(p−1)/12⌋. The displayed bound equals µ(m − 2δ − ε), which is valid but weaker. Since there are at most µ/6 ramification points, the "in particular" holds for every p ≥ 13; at p = 47 the count is 3µ. So this is a gap in the deduction, not a false statement, and it reaches nothing. The kind, affects, correction and reason are updated accordingly. I confirmed by hand that 47 is the only prime p ≥ 31 at which the displayed bound fails.

review.reason: Checked at pp.952–954 of the Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF (SHA-256 77ff3290…790e, the version named). The page images print "a Hecke character of order l^m" (p.952 and Proposition 3.3), "the conductor fl^m of ϕ̄ν" (p.953) and "let l^m be the conductor" (p.954). For l split, the part of the ring class group of conductor l^n coming from l is a quotient of (Z/l^n)^×. Its l-Sylow subgroup is cyclic of order l^{n−1} (the entry's "the l-part … of order (l−1)l^{n−1}" means the whole local factor). So a ν of exact order l^m ≥ l has conductor l^{m+1}O_K. Then L_m (degree l^m) does not lie in K(fl^m p^{n+1}), contrary to the definition of M_{n,m}, while z_{fl^m}, (3.6)–(3.7) and the proof of 3.3(3) all use l^m as the conductor. Reading l^m as the conductor and indexing L_m to match is consistent. So is the alternative of keeping "order" and using z_{fl^{m+1}}. Nothing else changes.

review.reason: Checked on the page image of p.960 of the Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF (SHA-256 77ff3290…790e, the version named). I verified the relation independently from Coleman's norm relation ∏_{w∈F[π]} f(X[+]w) = f([π]X). With h = f′/(fλ′), it gives Σ_{w∈F[π]} h(X[+]w) = π·h([π]X). At X = 0 this is Σ_{γ∈∆} h(v_0^γ) = (π − 1)h(0), so δ_1 = (1 − π^{−1})δ = (1 + p^{−1})δ. The trivial character has conductor p^0 and lies in Ξ⁺, so δ_1 vanishes on V^{∗,−}_∞, and hence so does δ. The same relation reconciles (3.6) with (3.7) through the Euler factor 1 − ϕ̄ν(pO_K)/p² = 1 + 1/p. It also shows that δ is well defined on V^∗_∞, since δ_1 kills (σ − 1)U^∗_∞.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 5.1(ii), p.956, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021), 943–966 (Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF, SHA-256 77ff3290…790e)
sourceIssues.printed: "(ii) Let A be an elliptic curve over O that is a lift of A̅. Then the Honda type of the associated formal group Â is ±x² + p. In particular, Â is Lubin–Tate with parameter ∓p." (with a_q(A̅) = ±2p)
sourceIssues.correction: "… the Honda type of Â is ∓x² + p. In particular, Â is Lubin–Tate with parameter ±p." That is, a_{p²} = 2p gives parameter p, and a_{p²} = −2p gives parameter −p.
sourceIssues.reason: By (i), φ_q = ±p on A̅ when a_q = ±2p. For a Lubin–Tate group with parameter π, [π] reduces to the q-power Frobenius. So π = φ_q = ±p, not ∓p. The paper's own set-up confirms this. §5.0.1 takes E/Q with a_p = 0, whose reduction has a_{p²} = a_p² − 2p = −2p, and states that Ê ≅ F, the Lubin–Tate group with parameter −p; the printed (ii) would give +p. Honda's type p − a_p x + x² for E/Z_p is x² + p there, whereas the printed (ii) would give −x² + p. The pairing of types with parameters in (ii) is right; only the link to the sign of a_q is reversed. Only "Â is Lubin–Tate" is used afterwards (p.958), so nothing is affected.
